Morning, George — it's Wednesday the nineteenth, and Athens has properly calmed down: still hot, but the wind's gone gentle.

Three things worth your attention.

The big child-safety trial against Meta just opened, with twenty-nine states arguing Instagram was built to hook kids — one to watch as a founder.

Overseas, Ukraine threw its heaviest drone barrage yet at Moscow.

And in AI, Stripe's buying OpenRouter for over seven billion.

— personal items —

Here's the rest.

Let's start with Ukraine, which launched its largest drone attack yet on the Russian capital — more than six hundred aimed at the Moscow region, over a hundred and eighty shot down overhead.

Russia hit back hard, striking a thermal power plant that had to stop generating and killing ten people in a Kharkiv village.

This war's widening, not winding down.

Then, in California, a trial that could reshape apps you use every day.

Twenty-nine states, led by California and Colorado, told an Oakland jury that Meta deliberately designed Instagram and Facebook to be addictive to minors — infinite scroll, the like button, all of it — and broke child-privacy law.

Meta says there's no proof anyone was actually harmed.

And your science hit is a lovely one.

Using a NASA X-ray telescope, astronomers found the strongest evidence yet for something called vacuum birefringence — a ninety-year-old prediction by Heisenberg that around a magnetar, empty space itself bends light.

It would mean the vacuum isn't truly empty.

One rival team still urges caution, but it's a genuine landmark.

On to tech, where the money's doing the talking.

Stripe, the payments giant, is buying OpenRouter — the service that lets developers switch between AI models — for more than seven billion dollars.

That's over five times what OpenRouter was worth just three months ago, and it turns AI model-routing into payment plumbing.

On the models themselves it's quiet: no new flagship overnight from OpenAI, Google, or xAI, and Claude's Opus 5 still sits on top.

One note for your own bills, though — Claude Sonnet's intro pricing ends the first of September.

Athens today: clear and hot, no rain in sight.

Around twenty-eight first thing, topping out near thirty-one mid-afternoon, back to twenty-six overnight.

The Meltemi's finally faded to a light northeast breeze, which is the good news — the catch is that calmer wind keeps the fire risk simmering, so stay clear of dry brush.

Sunset's just after eight.

To send you off a touch sharper.

World

  • Ukraine’s biggest strike yet on Moscow. Ukraine launched its largest drone attack of the war on the Russian capital — 600+ aimed at the Moscow region, with 180+ shot down overhead. Russia hit back, striking a DTEK thermal power plant that halted generation and killing 10 in a Kharkiv village. Kyiv Independent RBC-Ukraine
  • Meta’s child-safety trial opens. A bipartisan group of 29 states (led by California and Colorado) told an Oakland federal jury that Meta deliberately designed Instagram and Facebook to be addictive to minors — infinite scroll, the like button — and broke child-privacy law (COPPA). Meta says there’s no proof of harm. NPR NBC News
  • Science: “empty” space bends light. Using NASA’s IXPE X-ray telescope, astronomers found the strongest evidence yet for vacuum birefringence around a magnetar — a 90-year-old Heisenberg prediction that intense magnetic fields make the vacuum itself refract light. One independent team still urges caution. ScienceDaily Phys.org
